label: Human
plain: The law inventory names its candidate proteins by their human genes, so the human side of the protein atlas is the inventory's own.

modelled.text: Cells models a generic cell and a sheet of such cells, with laws whose candidate proteins are named by their human genes. No human cell type, organ or body is modelled: the heart and the body are placeholder outlines.

levels.note: The cell drawn is a generic animal cell, as one of a layer; it is not a model of a human cell type. Its shape and its sizes are the picture's choice: six flat sides where it meets its neighbours, about 20 µm across.

notes.text: A generic animal cell, as one of a layer
Its flat-sided shape is the picture's choice

levels.note: The sheet is the one Cells simulates: a single layer of coupled cells. It stands for no particular human tissue.

notes.text: The sheet Cells simulates: a single layer of coupled cells

levels.label: Heart
levels.note: The outline drawn is a human heart with its great vessels, as a placeholder. The heart is the picture's choice of organ: a paper on the injured heart is the user's high priority among the published models to reproduce (14 November 2026). No heart is modelled. The sheet of cells is drawn on the chest over the heart so that the scales follow one another; it is not heart tissue, and the heart's own cells are not modelled. The sizes are indicative.

sheet_mark.note: Here lies the sheet, 0.24 mm across: too small to see, so its ring is not to scale

notes.text: A human heart and its great vessels: a placeholder outline
The heart's own cells are not modelled

levels.label: Whole body
levels.note: The outline drawn is a human body lying on its back, 1.7 m long, as a placeholder. The sheet of cells is drawn on the chest for the scales only. The sizes are indicative, and the body's proportions are the picture's choice.

sheet_mark.note: Here lies the sheet: too small to see, so its ring is not to scale

notes.text: A human body: a placeholder outline

gray1918.text: Gray H (1918) Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th edition. The adult heart: about 12 cm long, 8 to 9 cm broad and 6 cm thick. Taken from a search digest of online copies of the text; the book itself was not opened.

ncdrisc2016.text: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (2016) A century of trends in adult human height. eLife 5:e13410. Mean adult heights from about 1.4 m to above 1.8 m, across countries and birth years. Taken from a search digest; the paper itself was not opened.
